title: Mastering Refractive Surgery: Clinical Pearls, Pitfalls, & Decision Making
summary: A comprehensive clinical guide for the refractive surgeon, covering preoperative screening, surgical nuance, and the management of challenging postoperative complications. Designed for residents and fellows to master the art and science of laser vision correction.

sections.title: The Refractive 'Red Flags'
content: Forme fruste keratoconus or topographic asymmetry
Uncontrolled autoimmune or connective tissue disease

content.explanation: S: Surface (Dry eye/Lid), T: Topography (Map), A: Age/Expectations, B: Bed (Residual thickness), L: Lens (Crystalline), E: Epithelium (Thickness/Map), R: Retina (Periphery check)

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always calculate 'Percent Tissue Altered' (PTA) > 40% risk factor for ectasia.
Use 0.02% Mitomycin-C for high-myopia PRK (> -6.00D) to prevent haze.
Warn patients with hyperopic shifts about 'night vision' issues (halos).
Never ignore 'asymmetric' bow-tie patterns on topography.
Monitor for DLK (Diffuse Lamellar Keratitis) on Day 1.

sections.title: Management of Post-op Complications
content: DLK (Sands of Sahara): Increase topical steroids (Pred Acetate 1% q1h) immediately.
Epithelial Ingrowth: Monitor; if encroaching visual axis or melting, lift flap and scrape.
Ectasia: Cross-linking (CXL) is the definitive treatment; do not re-laser.
Overcorrection: Wait 3-6 months; if stable, consider enhancement.

sections.title: Current Advances
content: SMILE (Small Incision Lenticule Extraction): Improved biomechanical stability over LASIK.
Topography-Guided Ablation: Optimized for irregular astigmatism.
Combined CXL + PRK (Athens Protocol) for keratoconus management.
AI-driven nomogram adjustments improving outcome predictability to within 0.25D.
